name: Strategy & Geopolitics
summary: AI is now treated as strategic infrastructure: chip controls swing between easing and tightening, states fund sovereign compute, militaries adopt AI-first plans, and power grids become a binding constraint.

regions.name: Compute, chips & export controls
regions.summary: The US opened case-by-case H200 sales to China in January 2026, yet shipments stalled; Blackwell stays barred and a May guidance tightened rules on Chinese firms' offshore units.
regions.whyItMatters: Who can buy frontier chips shapes which countries and companies can train and run the largest models.
regions.openQuestion: Will licensed H200 sales to China ever ship at scale, or do both governments now prefer decoupling?

landmarks.name: US opens case-by-case H200 sales to China
landmarks.summary: A BIS rule moved H200-class chips from presumed denial to case-by-case licence review for China, with volume caps and supply certifications, after Trump's offer tied to a 25% cut.

landmarks.name: Export enforcer: zero H200s sold to China
landmarks.summary: Commerce export enforcement chief David Peters told a House hearing on 24 February that, to his understanding, no H200s had yet gone to China.

landmarks.name: BIS targets Chinese firms' offshore units
landmarks.summary: Guidance issued on 31 May says licence requirements for advanced chips apply to entities headquartered in China even when located abroad, per Reuters.

deepDives.title: CNAS Insights: Unpacking the H200 Export Policy
deepDives.why: Think-tank analysis of what the January 2026 rule allows, its caps and its weak points.

deepDives.title: Mayer Brown: advanced AI chip policies codified
deepDives.why: Legal explainer of the BIS rule and the related 25% chip tariff proclamation.

regions.name: US-China competition
regions.summary: China is building a domestic AI stack on Huawei Ascend chips and open models, while the May 2026 Trump-Xi summit brought warm words but no settlement on chips or rare earths.
regions.whyItMatters: The two countries set the pace of frontier AI, and their rivalry drives chip rules, supply chains and model access worldwide.
regions.openQuestion: Can China's domestic chips sustain frontier training without Nvidia hardware?

landmarks.name: DeepSeek V4 adapted for Huawei chips
landmarks.summary: DeepSeek previewed V4-Pro and V4-Flash on 24 April; Huawei said V4 is supported on Ascend 950 clusters and that its chips were used for part of V4-Flash's training, per Reuters.

landmarks.name: Trump-Xi Beijing summit
landmarks.summary: The 14-15 May summit ended with warm words and few firm deals: no confirmed rare-earth fix, top Nvidia chips still restricted, and no extension of the trade truce, per Reuters.

landmarks.name: China's 15th Five-Year Plan elevates AI+
landmarks.summary: Approved by the National People's Congress in March 2026, the 2026-2030 plan mentions AI more than 50 times and stresses AI+ integration and technological self-reliance.

deepDives.title: ASPI Strategist: key takeaways from China's Two Sessions
deepDives.why: Short analytical read on what the new five-year plan signals for technology and security.

deepDives.title: ORF: reading the Trump-Xi summit
deepDives.why: Outside-view assessment of what the May 2026 summit did and did not change.

deepDives.title: China Briefing: what the summit agreed, and what not
deepDives.why: Itemised list of summit outcomes and the gaps between US and Chinese readouts.

regions.name: National AI strategies & sovereign AI
regions.summary: Governments from Canada to the Gulf and EU are funding domestic compute and models to reduce dependence on foreign providers, often through deals with US chipmakers.
regions.whyItMatters: Public money and state deals now decide where large AI clusters get built and who controls them.
regions.openQuestion: Does sovereign AI built on imported US chips and cloud software deliver real independence?

landmarks.name: Canada's 'AI for All' strategy
landmarks.summary: Launched by Mark Carney and AI minister Evan Solomon on 4 June, the six-pillar strategy includes building a sovereign AI foundation and reportedly more than C$2bn in spending.

landmarks.name: EU AI gigafactories tender
landmarks.summary: EuroHPC opened a tender on 30 July for up to seven AI gigafactories backed by up to EUR 10bn of EU and national funds; bids are due 3 December 2026 and 4 February 2027 by lot.

landmarks.name: Saudi Humain expands Nvidia deal
landmarks.summary: PIF-owned Humain announced up to 84MW of Nvidia compute, about 27,000 GPUs, in two phases through 2027; the later Vera Rubin phase is subject to final agreements.

landmarks.name: US Genesis Mission for AI in science
landmarks.summary: Executive Order 14363, signed 24 November 2025, directs the Energy Department to build a shared AI platform for scientific discovery across the national labs.

deepDives.title: Canada's national AI strategy (full text)
deepDives.why: The primary document: six pillars, funding lines and the build-partner-buy approach.

deepDives.title: European Commission: AI gigafactories
deepDives.why: Official page with the programme's aims, timeline and the 2025 expressions of interest.

deepDives.title: MoFo: the Genesis Mission executive order explained
deepDives.why: Plain summary of what the order requires of DOE and by when.

regions.name: International governance & safety institutes
regions.summary: Global AI governance has shifted to broad, nonbinding forums: the India summit, a new UN scientific panel and dialogue, and an annual international safety science report.
regions.whyItMatters: These forums are the only places where most governments, including the US and China, discuss AI risk together.
regions.openQuestion: Can nonbinding declarations and science panels constrain frontier developers, or only describe what they do?

landmarks.name: International AI Safety Report 2026
landmarks.summary: Published 3 February and chaired by Yoshua Bengio, the second report finds continued capability gains and a widening gap between safety testing and real-world behaviour.

landmarks.name: New Delhi Declaration at AI Impact Summit
landmarks.summary: Eighty-six countries and two international organisations, including the US, UK, EU and China, endorsed a voluntary, nonbinding declaration on collaborative and inclusive AI.

landmarks.name: First UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance
landmarks.summary: The first Dialogue met in Geneva on 6-7 July, informed by the UN scientific panel's preliminary report; the second is set for New York on 3-4 May 2027.

deepDives.title: International AI Safety Report 2026: extended summary
deepDives.why: The report's own policymaker summary of capabilities, risks and safeguards.

deepDives.title: UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance: FAQ
deepDives.why: How the Dialogue and the scientific panel work, who takes part and what comes next.

deepDives.title: Covington: what the 2026 safety report covers
deepDives.why: Lawyer's digest of the report's main findings for readers short on time.

regions.name: Defense & military AI
regions.summary: The Pentagon adopted an AI-first strategy and fought Anthropic in court over a supply chain risk label, while Ukraine pushes battlefield AI but says full integration is years away.
regions.whyItMatters: Militaries are becoming major AI customers, and the terms they set test how far labs can restrict use of their models.
regions.openQuestion: Can an AI lab keep usage limits on its models once a government treats them as defence infrastructure?

landmarks.name: Pentagon AI Acceleration Strategy
landmarks.summary: Hegseth's January strategy aims for an 'AI-first' warfighting force, sets seven pace-setting projects and wants frontier models deployed within 30 days of public release.

landmarks.name: Court rules Anthropic risk label unlawful
landmarks.summary: A California federal judge ruled on 27 August that the Pentagon's supply chain risk label for Anthropic was unlawful; a separate DC case went the other way.

landmarks.name: Ukraine bets on battlefield AI
landmarks.summary: Defense AI Center head Danylo Tsvok told AP that AI is a matter of national survival and that full battlefield integration may take three to five years.

deepDives.title: Release of the War Department's AI Acceleration Strategy
deepDives.why: The department's own release of the strategy, for reading the text rather than coverage.

deepDives.title: Nextgov: DOD's AI acceleration strategy
deepDives.why: Commentary on what the strategy changes in practice and where it may fall short.

deepDives.title: Small Wars Journal: Ukraine bets on AI
deepDives.why: Practitioner-oriented take on Ukraine's battlefield AI programme.

regions.name: Energy & data centres
regions.summary: Data centre electricity use is forecast to rise about a quarter in 2026, pushing hyperscalers into nuclear deals and making grids such as PJM a constraint on AI buildout.
regions.whyItMatters: Power, not chips, is increasingly what limits how fast AI capacity can be added and who pays for it.
regions.openQuestion: Who bears the grid and bill costs if data centre demand forecasts prove too high, or too low?

landmarks.name: Gartner: data centre power up 26% in 2026
landmarks.summary: Gartner forecasts global data centre electricity use of 565TWh in 2026, up from 447TWh in 2025, driven by AI-optimised servers.

landmarks.name: Meta backs up to 6.6GW of nuclear power
landmarks.summary: Deals announced on 9 January with Vistra, Oklo and TerraPower cover existing plants and planned advanced reactors; Meta says they could support up to 6.6GW by 2035.

landmarks.name: BNEF: data centres a fifth of US power by 2035
landmarks.summary: BloombergNEF projects data centres at about 20% of US electricity use by 2035, up from about 6% now, with the share in the PJM grid reported at roughly a third.

deepDives.title: Gartner: data centre electricity forecast 2026
deepDives.why: Headline TWh and GW forecasts to 2030 and the split between AI and conventional servers.

deepDives.title: World Nuclear News: Meta's nuclear agreements
deepDives.why: Industry-press detail on each deal: plants, megawatts and target dates.

regions.name: Elections & information integrity
regions.summary: The 2026 US midterms saw heavy spending on AI-generated political ads, mostly without disclaimers; rules are a patchwork of state labelling laws and few voters yet use chatbots.
regions.whyItMatters: Elections are the most visible test of whether synthetic media and chatbots change what voters believe.
regions.openQuestion: Did AI-generated ads and chatbot answers measurably shift votes, or mainly erode trust in what is real?

landmarks.name: AI-generated ads in US midterms
landmarks.summary: The Wesleyan Media Project tracked well over $100m of spending on AI-generated or AI-enhanced political ads in 2026 races; only about 27% carried an AI disclaimer.

landmarks.name: State AI ad laws fail to ensure disclosure
landmarks.summary: AP reported that AI ads were popular in the midterms while state labelling laws, reportedly in 31 states, had not stopped a lack of disclosure; there is no federal rule.

landmarks.name: Few voters use chatbots for election info
landmarks.summary: A Pew survey of 5,273 US adults in October found 8% using AI chatbots for 2026 election information, rising to 11% of those under 50.

deepDives.title: Wesleyan Media Project: AI in political ads
deepDives.why: The research group's own running counts of AI ad spending, sponsors and disclaimers.

deepDives.title: Pew: chatbots and 2026 election information
deepDives.why: Survey data on who asks chatbots about elections and what they ask for.

deepDives.title: States United: how well AI answers voter questions
deepDives.why: Tests of AI platforms' answers to practical voting questions.

regions.name: Open vs closed models
regions.summary: Chinese labs keep releasing strong open-weight models and are reported to lead open-model usage, while Meta moved its newest frontier model to closed weights.
regions.whyItMatters: Open weights decide who can run and adapt capable models without permission, including outside the US.
regions.openQuestion: Will US labs keep releasing competitive open weights, or cede that layer to Chinese developers?

landmarks.name: Meta launches closed Muse Spark
landmarks.summary: The first model from Meta Superintelligence Labs shipped on 8 April with no public weights, a break from Llama; Meta said future versions may be open-sourced.

landmarks.name: DeepSeek V4 released as open weights
landmarks.summary: DeepSeek posted V4-Pro and V4-Flash on Hugging Face on 24 April, keeping its flagship models openly downloadable a year after its first breakout release.

landmarks.name: Chinese models dominate open-weight usage
landmarks.summary: Analyses of OpenRouter data put Chinese open-weight models at roughly 61% of routed tokens by May 2026, led by Qwen, DeepSeek, GLM and Kimi.
landmarks.note: Single VC analysis; figure not re-checked this pass (search budget ran out).

landmarks.name: MIT Tech Review on China's open-source lead
landmarks.summary: Reporting examines how Chinese open models overtook US ones in downloads and why US policymakers now see open weights as a strategic issue.
landmarks.note: Plausible and important; article could not be opened or searched this pass.

regions.name: Domestic AI regulation
regions.summary: The EU delayed AI Act high-risk rules to 2027-28 via a digital omnibus, and the US White House moved to preempt state AI laws through litigation and funding conditions.
regions.whyItMatters: These rules set the compliance burden for anyone building or deploying AI in the two largest Western markets.
regions.openQuestion: Will delay and preemption produce simpler rules, or a long gap with few binding rules at all?

landmarks.name: EU agrees AI Act omnibus delay
landmarks.summary: Provisional deal moves high-risk obligations to December 2027 and August 2028 and adds a ban on nudification apps.
landmarks.note: Not re-checked this pass (search budget ran out); marked verified by the earlier pass.

landmarks.name: US order targets state AI laws
landmarks.summary: A December 2025 executive order created a DOJ AI Litigation Task Force, formed in January 2026, and tied broadband funds to state AI rules; its legality is contested.
landmarks.note: Not re-checked this pass (search budget ran out); marked verified by the earlier pass.
